text:
Where are you now? You were so sweet, child,

with blond hair and eyes of steel…

Child who, despite myself, was my prisoner,

O my pale child!


So humble was the kiss that kissed my feet,

with such deep delight, with such limpid complaint,

that as time passes and moves away

my feet desire it.


You would fall silent on golden afternoons

when a book in our hands brought us sadness,

and then your head would fall upon my knees

like a flake of gold.


Then perfumes rose from your soul

to the tired soul that weighed upon my breast…

O your soul… as fresh as a fern branch!

It rose in perfumes.


Child whom I adored… O your white tears

that watered the impossible word in abundance,

I was your discreet sister, sad and sensitive child,

of white tears.


I loved no one as I loved you, sweet and somber child

who wept in my arms over my prudent turning away.

My memory will love you without end,

sweet and somber child.


Let us go toward the trees… Sleep

will come upon us by celestial grace.

Let us go toward the trees; the night

will be soft for us, sadness light.


Let us go toward the trees, the soul

drowsed by wild perfume,

but be quiet, do not speak, be merciful;

do not wake the sleeping birds.

translation.title: Sweet and Somber
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's intimate address, the repeated end-words of its quatrains, and the final movement into a hushed forest.
